verdict.headline: Government bond selloff turns global as Japan's 10-year hits a level unseen since 1996
verdict.label: Synchronized sovereign repricing: JGB 10Y at 3% (first since 1996) with the 5Y at a record 2.26%, 30Y gilt 5.89% (highest since May 1998), Bund 10Y 3.36%, UST 10Y 4.81% (highest since November 2023) and 30Y 5.286%. Brent $94.86 after US drones struck anchored Iranian tankers across ~100 targets; Iran fired on a US base in Jordan. VIX 16.34 (+9.5%), gold -1.86% Tuesday, DXY ~99.5. Futures lower into the 8:15 ADP print (consensus ~47K).
verdict.rationale_short: Tuesday's read held: oil pushes inflation up, so rates go up. What changed is scope. Long-dated government bonds are being sold in Japan, the UK, Germany and the US at the same time, so investors are demanding more to hold long-term bonds anywhere, not just in one country. Two causes are adding together: oil, which raises inflation expectations and points to tighter policy everywhere, and roughly $132 billion of long-dated hyperscaler bond issuance competing with governments for the same buyers. Confirmation is still absent: the 30-year has traded above 5.30% twice and closed there neither time, and futures price the September hike at 66% against 26% on Kalshi. A 30-year close above 5.30% or Brent through $100 extends the frame; a 10-year back under 4.70% with the S&P reclaiming 7,700 dissolves it.

supporting_data.label: JGB 10Y reached 3% for the first time since 1996 and the 5Y hit a record 2.26%; 10Y gilts rose 11bps to 5.25% with the 30Y at 5.89%, highest since May 1998, and the Bund 10Y touched 3.36%
US 10-year Treasury yield touched 4.81%, its highest since November 2023; the 30-year rose 2bps to 5.286%
Fed funds futures price September hike odds above 66% while Kalshi prices a hold at 73% and a hike at 26% — an unusually wide split into the September 16 meeting
US drones struck anchored Iranian government tankers across roughly 100 targets under a new 'tanker for tanker' policy — the first tanker strike in retaliation rather than blockade enforcement
Hyperscalers issued roughly $132 billion of bonds through July 2026 against $109 billion in all of 2025 and $20 billion in 2024, weighted to maturities of five years and longer
Dell Q2 revenue a record $47.0B (+58%) with EPS $7.04 vs $4.87 consensus, FY27 revenue guidance raised $25B to ~$192B, and AI server backlog at a record $95B

watchlist_mentions.note: Brent at $94.86 has held above $94 through the escalation, supplying the inflation impulse behind the global yield move. US drones hit the engine rooms of anchored Iranian government tankers, which targets export capacity directly; loadings and voluntary transit suspensions, not strike counts, are what would convert this into a measured supply disruption.
Gold fell 1.86% to $4,358.74 for a third consecutive session while US forces struck Iranian tankers — the sign that markets are pricing inflation and bond supply rather than fear.
The dollar held near 99.5 and barely moved on the escalation, consistent with gold: no haven bid is being paid on geopolitical headlines while the rate path is repricing.
Traded $76,988 (-1.6%) after opening at $77,395.89 and reaching $76,597, leaving the $76,661 support inside the day's range for a second session.
At 16.34, up 9.52%, against a 2026 low of 14.13 set on August 31 — an event premium now exists where there was none two sessions ago. Reported as data, not as a regime trigger.
Closed at 7,631.47, below the 7,650 level flagged Tuesday, with futures lower pre-open and the Nasdaq leading again. 7,580-7,700 is the range that holds if one afternoon completed the adjustment.

trade_setups.thesis: The long bond has traded above 5.30% in two separate sessions and closed there in neither, sitting at 5.286%. What is different now is that the bid it would need is global: gilts at 5.89% and JGBs at 3% are competing for the same duration buyers, and Treasury's long-dated buyback operations do not begin until September 9.
trade_setups.entry: A daily close above 5.30% marks the level crossed rather than tagged; a close under 5.15% says the buyback bid is being anticipated
trade_setups.invalidation: Brent back under $90 or a payrolls print under 150K removes the inflation impulse driving the move
trade_setups.horizon: This week, with Friday's jobs report the decisive test

trade_setups.thesis: Fed funds futures price a hike at above 66% while Kalshi prices one at 26% and a hold at 73%. A gap that wide between the two venues is a dispersion that resolves rather than persists, and this week's labour data is what resolves it. ADP is due at 8:15 AM ET with consensus near 47,000 against 44,000 in July, the weakest in six months.
trade_setups.entry: A print under 30,000 alongside an unchanged inflation impulse is the stagflation combination in its clearest form; above 70,000 closes the gap the hawkish way
trade_setups.invalidation: A Beige Book showing districts absorbing rather than passing through oil costs weakens the hawkish side of the split

trade_setups.thesis: The strike pattern changed from escort and mine-laying capability to export capacity: US drones hit the engine rooms of anchored Iranian government tankers under a stated 'tanker for tanker' policy. Crude has nonetheless held near $94.86 rather than extending, because transit through Hormuz has not stopped.
trade_setups.entry: Iranian loadings and voluntary transit suspensions by major operators put $100 in play; a return under $90 says the premium is decaying on July's schedule
trade_setups.invalidation: A confirmed halt in hostilities or a return to the June deal framework collapses the risk premium built over four sessions
trade_setups.horizon: Days; the exchange has run on 24-36 hour cycles

bear_case: The read treats a common input as a regime change. Four government bond markets selling off together is what happens when one global input, oil, moves. It is not proof that investors will permanently demand more to hold long-term bonds, and September issuance windows reliably thin the bid in exactly this week of the year. The hawkish pricing is also thinner than it looks: futures at 66% sit against Kalshi's 73% hold, and a labour market whose openings were revised down 177,000 will not sustain that pricing through a soft payrolls print. If the 10-year closes back under 4.70% and the S&P reclaims 7,700, this read no longer holds.
